ambiguity: Easily interchangeable with two-arrow sync/cycle icons, undo/counter-clockwise arrows, or recurring-task status indicators.
task_intents: factory reset a device or router
renew an expiring subscription or license
redo a failed step or experiment
turn or rotate household items seasonally

example_tasks.task: Rotate all sideways scans in the 1998 family album folder
Reset the garage keypad code before the dog sitter starts
Restart staging worker after the midnight migration finishes
Rotate living room monstera a quarter turn toward the south window
Flush DNS cache and reload local proxy rules on work laptop
Before handing over at Apple Store
Hard reset the espresso machine descale counter so the orange light stops blinking
Redo the sourdough bulk ferment at 24C instead of leaving it on the cold counter

Write down router settings before hitting the pinhole reset

Renew passport at the post office before June
Pay the recurring monthly HOA fee

reasoning: A single clockwise circular arrow universally read as refresh, reload, rotate clockwise, reset, or redo. It is an abstract action/UI glyph rather than a concrete noun, so it fits best when resetting, rebooting, rotating, or redoing is the primary point of the task, while tasks with strong physical nouns (tires, passports) should use their object icon instead.
